name: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam
title: Ancient Trees in Amsterdam's Hortus Botanicus
meta_description: Amsterdam's 1638 botanical garden holds the country's oldest and thickest Turkish hazel, plus an evergreen Turner's oak.
intro: The Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam has been growing rare plants on the same corner of the Plantage since 1638. A Turkish hazel planted in 1795, the country's oldest and thickest according to the Dutch tree foundation, flowers with pollen-shedding catkins every January while the rest of the garden sits bare. A few paths over, a Turner's oak keeps its leathery leaves through the whole Dutch winter, evergreen in a garden that otherwise goes bare. Both stand a few minutes' walk apart, on the one Hortus ticket. Three more of the garden's monumental trees, a corkscrewing catalpa, a shellbark hickory and a ginkgo, are fully researched but currently held off this list because they sit behind that same ticket alongside a third of Amsterdam's other trees; they return the day the balance of paid to free trees allows it.
